caption:
A new report says 94% of senior executives are open to leaving their jobs.

That number isn't about compensation. It's the statistical shadow of being unheard in the room — the idea ignored until a peer repeats it, the promotion that goes sideways, the meeting where you were present but not counted.

A new company doesn't fix that. You carry the same bearing through the new door, into the same silence.

Command isn't a title someone hands you. It's built: how you hold the room, how you use your voice, when you choose not to fill the space. Thirty-five years of military command taught Colonel Suhag that authority is a practiced discipline, not a personality trait.

Before you update the résumé, audit the presence. One of those two changes everything.

topic.title: 94% of senior leaders open to leaving their jobs
topic.angle: Lumina's audience isn't short on ability — they're short on recognition, and a stat showing 94% of senior executives are mentally halfway out the door is the statistical shadow of being unheard in the room, which changing companies doesn't fix.
topic.why_now: The report was published 9–10 September 2026 — four to five days old — and is being picked up across multiple outlets simultaneously, landing inside senior-role interview and mobility season.

rationale: A stark, text-only stat card matches the caption's direct, no-nonsense argument and lets the 94% figure carry the weight without decorative distraction.
